content: Bromhexine is a mucolytic agent, also known as an expectorant, that is utilized in the management of respiratory disorders characterized by the presence of thick or excessive mucus. Additionally, bromhexine exhibits antioxidant properties. Bromhexine functions by enhancing the body’s natural mechanisms for clearing mucus from the respiratory tract. It acts as a secretolytic agent, promoting the production of serous mucus in the respiratory tract. This process reduces the viscosity of phlegm, making it thinner and less sticky. By doing so, bromhexine facilitates a secretomotoric effect, aiding the cilia in transporting mucus out of the lungs. For this reason, bromhexine is frequently included in cough syrups. Bromhexine is a synthetic derivative of vasicine, a compound derived from herbal sources. It has been demonstrated to increase the proportion of serous bronchial secretions, thereby making the mucus easier to expel. It is specifically indicated for use as a secretolytic therapy in bronchopulmonary diseases associated with abnormal mucus secretion and impaired mucus transport. Bromhexine is available in various formulations to suit patient needs. These include highand low-strength syrups (8 mg/5 ml and 4 mg/5 ml), tablets and soluble tablets (both containing 8 mg of bromhexine), and oral solutions (10 mg/5 ml). The dosage regimen is tailored according to the patient’s age and weight, with products available for all age groups, including infants. Bromhexine is a well-established and well-tolerated medication. In some cases, it is replaced by its active metabolite, ambroxol, which is found in products such as Mucosolvan or Mucangin.
